newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cabinet approves 2.67 trln yen extra budget.
newsitem.headline: Japan cabinet approves 2.67 trln yen extra budget.

text.p: Japan's cabinet on Friday approved a draft supplementary budget totalling 2.67 trillion yen for the year ending next March 31, the Finance Ministry said.
The extra budget will fund spending on restructuring in areas around Kobe in western Japan which were hit by a massive earthquake in 1995 and measures to cope with natural disasters.

It will also cover costs to cope with the aftermath of a massive food poisoning outbreak during the summer as well as measures taken to help farmers deal with liberalisation of farm trade after a global trade agreement in 1993.

The budget will also include 7.2 billion yen for feasibility studies related to the Special Action Committee on Okinawa, a team of U.S. and Japanese defence officials discussing the scaling back of U.S. military bases in Okinawa.
Another 5.0 billion yen will be used to study what steps can be taken to help boost the Okinawan economy.

The ministry plans to fund the extra budget with tax revenues worth 391 billion yen and 32.2 billion yen of non-tax revenues. The shortfall will be made up by about 1.34 trillion yen worth of bond issues and 904.1 billion yen in carryover money from 1995/96. The extra budget will be submitted to the parliament session starting in January.
